back: The informal, community-based preparation of children for adult life in traditional society, through watching and taking part.
Knowledge such as history, stories and proverbs passed on by speaking and remembering.

front: Who were the teachers in indigenous education?
back: Parents, grandparents, aunts, uncles, elders and the whole community.

front: Name four methods of indigenous education.
back: Observation, participation, folk tales and proverbs (also songs, riddles and initiation).

front: What is a folk tale called in Shona and in Ndebele?
Name four areas of content in indigenous education.
back: Practical skills, values, history and identity, and religion.

front: Why was religion not a separate subject in traditional education?
back: Religion and morality were part of daily life, taught through ritual, taboos, stories and example.

front: Give two strengths of indigenous education.
back: It was practical and relevant, and it taught values and unity at no cost.

front: Give two limitations of indigenous education.
back: Knowledge relied on memory and could be lost, and it offered no qualifications or outside scientific knowledge.
